facts.text: The South Bronx was originally known as the Manor of Morrisania, named after Lewis Morris.
An apartment building at 1520 Sedgwick Avenue is recognized as the birthplace of hip hop, where DJ Kool Herc held pivotal parties.
The Zulu Nation was founded in the South Bronx to promote peace, love, and unity as an alternative to street violence.
The Fashion Moda Gallery in the South Bronx helped launch the careers of artists like Keith Haring and Jenny Holzer.
The Bronx County Courthouse and much of the Grand Concourse are recognized for their distinct Art Deco architecture.
Early populations of the South Bronx grew as German and Irish immigrants began to settle in the area.
